how does the swing desk decide what to buy

Right now (Stage 1) it uses momentum. At 3:45pm it lines up every stock it's considering, its watchlist plus up to 30 strong, affordable names from the daily scan, and ranks them by how much they rose over the past 12 months, leaving out the latest month. A stock in the top 20% that's also above its 200-day average is a buy, strongest first, while there are free slots (8 in total) and cash. If SPY itself is under its 200-day average, it holds what it has and buys nothing new.

how do i turn on the autopilot

Open Setup → Autopilot and press Turn on. It runs the bot in the background: it starts when you log in and restarts itself if it stops. The tag next to Autopilot shows on, off, or "on · not running", and a "Last problem" line appears if it stopped recently. The pill at the top of the window shows "Autopilot running" and when it last checked in. Keep the Mac plugged in, and turn on lid-closed mode just below if you want to close the lid.

is the momentum strategy guaranteed to make money?

No. Nothing in trading is guaranteed, and Kestrel's own research says so. Momentum has real-world support, but a real momentum fund beat SPY by only about a point or two a year since 2013, with bigger drops. In the 16-year test, even the best method failed a 30-day "make money and beat SPY" check about 4 times in 10. Kestrel's safety rules (stops, budget caps, the kill switch) limit losses; they don't create gains. Past results don't guarantee future results.

what tags does it record on a buy

The stock itself ('buying NIO'). A stock under $5. On the day desk: whether it was a stock in play or from the fixed list, and whether it was bought in the first 30 minutes or after 2pm. Chasing: on the day desk, already up 3% or more since the open; on the swing desk, up 10% or more in 5 days. Moving with a stock it already owns. And option bets against it. These tags are what the mistake memory groups trades by.

do i need to worry about the pattern day trader rule with only $50?

Not at Alpaca: Alpaca dropped the old $25k day-trading rule on June 4, 2026, and Kestrel's safety notes say FINRA retired the rule. With a small account the limit that matters is settlement instead. At Schwab, treated as a cash account, Kestrel only spends settled money, which with $50 means about one full round trip per day at most. At Alpaca, sale money is usable right away.

can kestrel text me when it buys or sells something

Yes. Set up Telegram in Setup → Your phone and your private Kestrel bot messages you every buy and sell, with what it spent, what it got back and whether it was a win or a loss, plus the after-close results, the after-market report and anything urgent like a pause or the kill switch. If you'd rather have push notifications, add Pushover in the same section; it sends every buy and sell too. You can use both. The Mac sends them, so it needs to be awake and online.

what does why it moved show

On a stock's card (click any ticker) and in the after-market report: how much it moved today and over the last 5 trading days, next to the latest headlines (with source and time) and SEC filings. The report lists what it owns and any of the scan's top picks that moved 3% or more. It's a hint, not proof: news can follow a move as well as cause it.

when does the swing desk actually make its trades?

Once a day, 15 minutes before the close: 3:45pm New York time on a normal day, 12:45pm on early-close days. That's when it scores its stocks and places buys and sells. The rest of the trading day the autopilot still checks the swing positions every 5 minutes, but only for stop-losses. It decides near the close because its backtest decides and fills at each day's close, and the same code runs in testing, paper and live, so what was tested is what trades.

why did the swing desk sell something

One of four things: the 7% stop-loss was hit; momentum's score fell below 0.5, meaning the stock dropped out of the top half of its ranking; the stock fell below its 200-day average (its score goes to 0); or it was a trim because one stock grew to more than twice its 12.5% share. Every sale has its reason written next to it in the Activity list and the journal, so you can see which one it was. The market falling below its 200-day average doesn't force sales; it just stops new buys.

what's the relapse rule

Lessons fade after 60 days unless they're confirmed again, so the bot can notice when things change. But it remembers which lessons it learned. If a faded lesson's situation loses again later, the lesson comes back at once, without needing another 3 or 8 losing trades. The reason reads like 'lost again (ticker on date) after it had learned this once'.

what if the internet cuts out right when it's placing an order?

The bot stops tracking an order only once the broker confirms it's finished (filled, cancelled, rejected or expired). If the broker can't confirm, it does nothing risky and checks again next cycle. Orders are written down the moment they're sent. At Alpaca and Webull they're written down with the bot's own tag before sending, so after a restart it can ask the broker whether it got that order. If an order went out but no order id came back, it tells you to check your account by hand.

should i pay for alpaca's $99 a month data?

Not for what Kestrel does today. In Kestrel's notes, $99/month is Alpaca's full options feed. The options-gap watcher only needs each contract's daily volume once a day, which Alpaca's free feed has (15 minutes late), and the watcher never trades anyway. For stock prices, the free IEX feed is real-time but covers one exchange (about 2-3% of volume): prices track the market closely, volumes are smaller. The stocks-in-play check compares IEX with IEX, so it stays like for like. All-exchange data needs Alpaca's paid plan.

alpaca, schwab or webull, which one should i use?

They differ in practical ways, and all three use the same safety rules. Alpaca: paper and real money with the same code, fractional shares, no good faith violations, and it's where the $50 real-money test starts. Schwab: real money only (no paper trading), whole shares only, cash-account rules, and you log in again every 7 days. Webull: a paper (test server) account and real money, whole shares for now, cash-account rules by default, and an approval in the Webull app. Paper can run at Alpaca or Webull, or be simulated on your Mac.

what's danger news

When news is on, the bot reads recent headlines (the last 3 days) from Alpaca's news feed, or Yahoo without keys. If a stock's headlines contain words like offering, bankrupt, chapter 11, trading halt, delist, going concern, SEC charges, fraud, reverse split, default, restatement or subpoena, it won't buy that stock for now. Stocks in play with danger news are skipped too. News never makes it buy anything; it only keeps it away.

why isn't it buying anything?

Several rules can stop new buys, and the after-market report lists the reason under its thinking. Common ones: all slots are full (8 swing, 3 day); SPY is below its 200-day average (momentum then buys nothing new); the desk is down more than 3% today; a strong stock has danger news or, on the swing desk, an earnings report within 3 trading days; the Risk agent is skipping a repeated mistake; the strategy has been paused by its own lessons; or it's the day desk's last 30 minutes. Sometimes nothing simply scores high enough.

explain tjr strategy in simple terms

The idea: big moves often start with a fake-out. Price drops just below an obvious low, which triggers other traders' stop-losses, then turns around and breaks back up. Kestrel waits for that whole sequence on 5-minute bars: hourly trend up, a dip below yesterday's low or a recent swing low, then a close above the last swing high. It buys on the pullback into the price gap the move left, only from 9:35 to 11:30am, with a stop just under the dip and a target of 2 times the risk.

can i approve the trading plan or switch to real money from the app window

Not from the window. Approving a study plan and moving a desk to real money stay in the full Setup menu in Terminal, where each big step needs a typed confirmation: YES to approve a plan, REAL MONEY to promote a desk. Open it with Kestrel → Setup Menu (keys, plans, autopilot)…, ⌘, or the Full Setup menu… button in Setup. Real money also needs every paper rule to pass and LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true in ~/AITrader/.env.

what's the difference between webull paper keys and real money keys?

They're separate keys for separate servers: Webull's paper (test) keys only work on its test server, and real-money keys only on its real server. Setup asks which kind you pasted, and if you pick wrong, Test Webull finds out and switches. Paper trading at Webull needs the paper keys and Paper trading happens at: Webull. Real money at Webull needs real-money keys, Broker for real money: Webull, and the same locks as elsewhere: passing paper results, LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true and your typed REAL MONEY.

when does the after market report come out and where do i find it

About 25 minutes after each close (New York time), as long as the autopilot is on. It's at the top of the Journal tab under After-market report, with a date picker for the last week. It's also saved on your Mac in ~/AITrader/data/reports/ as after-market-<date>.md, and python run.py report prints it. If Telegram is paired, you get the whole report there; with Pushover you get its summary. Telegram's /report command sends it on request.

what has to happen before kestrel can trade my real money?

Four locks all have to be open, and each desk (swing and day) earns it separately. 1) The desk's paper results pass the promotion rules: at least 30 trading days of paper trading, it made money, it beat SPY over the same days, and it never dropped more than 10% from its best day. 2) Your ~/AITrader/.env file says LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true. 3) Prices are real-time, meaning Alpaca or Schwab data, not free Yahoo data. 4) You run the promote step and type REAL MONEY exactly. If any one is missing, no real order goes out.

what local ai model does kestrel use

Google's Gemma 4 12B (gemma4:12b in Ollama), about an 8 GB download. It writes the plain-English parts: the plan, the after-market report's summary and the team's notes; it never decides trades. A Mac with less than 16 GB of memory uses the small Qwen3 4B (qwen3:4b, about 2.5 GB) instead, so the AI never slows down trading. Setup → AI & news shows which one your Mac uses.

what if my mac was asleep at 3:45

Then the swing desk misses that day's decision, and after the close the journal warns that it missed it. Positions in a broker account are still protected by stop orders resting at the broker. The day desk's resting stops expire that night, and any day position left over is sold at its first cycle the next morning. That's why the bot only works properly while the Mac is awake, online and plugged in.

why did it buy NIO

NIO is on the day desk's fixed watchlist, so any buy came from the day desk's method. Every buy carries its reason, like the method's name and 'score 1.00 >= 0.9', in the Activity list and the journal, and the after-market report shows what it traded, why, and the team's notes on that decision. If the desk was practicing TJR's model, a score of 1.0 means the full setup happened: hourly trend up, a sweep, a break above the swing high and a pullback into the gap. Check the journal entry for that day for the exact reason.

what's opening_range_breakout

A day-desk method. The first 30 minutes after the open set the day's opening range, and it has no opinion while that range forms. After that, it buys if the price breaks above the range's high and exits if the price falls back below the middle of the range. Like every day trade, anything still open is sold 10 minutes before the close.

the backtest says momentum made 40% a year?? so that's what we'll get?

No. The 40.5% a year is flattered. The test's stock list only holds companies that survived and are popular today, and that hurts momentum most, since it buys stocks that went up, and in a survivors-only list those are the ones that kept going. A real momentum fund, MTUM, made about 15.6-16% a year since 2013, against 14.4% for SPY over the same span. The honest expectation is the market plus 1-2 points a year, with bigger drops.
